public_rationale: Exxact's June 10, 2026 benchmarks document molecular dynamics on B200, GH200 and H100 GPUs [e1]. June 2026 preprints report quantum-circuit and many-body simulations on H100 systems, and finite-element material mechanics on A100 and H100 GPUs [e2, e3]. These working applications demonstrate substantial usefulness across several non-generative fields within the April–June reporting window, contradicting the claim of little usefulness beyond generative AI [e1, e2, e3]. Exxact's warning about purchase-price efficiency limits the cost-effectiveness conclusion, not the demonstrated ability to perform molecular dynamics [e1].
limitations: Exxact is a hardware vendor; the other two sources are preprints.
The research publication dates do not separately establish when each experimental run occurred.
The evidence does not measure commercial workload shares or demand sufficient to absorb GPUs after an investment collapse.
The results do not establish cost effectiveness for every workload or usefulness across every accelerator architecture.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: AI GPUs are useful for generative AI and little else.

statement.excerpt: Newsflash! AI GPUs are useful for generative AI and not much else.

our_interpretation: AI GPUs means data-center GPUs used for AI workloads, including A100, H100, and B200-class hardware.
The ordinary reading is that these GPUs have few substantial useful applications outside generative AI. It does not require non-generative workloads to dominate GPU sales or utilization.
For this ongoing capability claim, I use April through June 2026, the latest completed quarter before publication, as the reporting window.
Demonstrated scientific computation counts as useful even when another GPU offers better purchase-price performance. Merely theoretical compatibility is insufficient.
criteria.support_condition: Representative evidence establishes that useful applications outside generative AI are narrow or marginal on AI data-center GPUs.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Documented working applications establish substantial usefulness across several non-generative fields on AI data-center GPUs.

evidence.explanation: The published benchmark documents molecular dynamics workloads on B200, GH200, and H100 GPUs, including a million-atom system. Its purchase-cost caveat is material: demonstrated usefulness does not establish that these are the cheapest GPUs for that work.

evidence.excerpt: All experiments use DGX H100 nodes (Section II-D).
evidence.explanation: The experiments demonstrate quantum circuit simulation and three many-body dynamics workloads on H100 systems, with scaling across multiple nodes. These are numerical scientific computations rather than generative AI applications.
